title: This emulator reimagines Nintendo’s Virtual Boy with a full color display
gist: VBoy Color is a new Virtual Boy emulator. Its game-specific Color Packs give each 8x8 tile its own four-color palette, turning Nintendo's red-on-black 1990s headset games into Game Boy Color-style full-color scenes. The beta ships packs for 15 games and has VR/3D stereoscopic support, but tile coloring sometimes misses tiles and does not work on wireframe games.

insights.claim: The VBoy Color emulator does not just swap the Virtual Boy's four shades of red for four other colors. Its game-specific Color Packs give each 8x8 tile in a scene its own four-color palette, so objects that shared the same red hues on original hardware can appear in many different colors.

insights.claim: In the current VBoy Color beta, the coloring algorithm sometimes misses individual tiles, leaving flickering uncolored squares. Tile coloring also does not work on wireframe 3D games such as 3-D Tetris or Red Alarm, which instead get depth-based palettes or gradients.

insights.so_what: The tool is still immature, so treat it as a hobbyist project rather than a polished product.

insights.claim: VBoy Color builds on earlier emulators VirtualBoyGo and Beetle VB and supports full stereoscopic display on VR headsets and 3D monitors. Kyle Orland sees it as part of a trend of emulators that improve on the experience of the original hardware.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: VR headsets are finding a niche as a way to play retro 3D hardware games.
